title: MANICOUAGAN EYE

beats.text: This circular lake is seventy kilometers wide, and a five‑kilometer meteor created it.
From orbit it looks like a bright blue eye surrounded by dark rings.
The inner water ring spans seventy kilometers, while the whole crater reaches about one hundred kilometers.
So what caused this perfect circular lake to form?
A five-kilometer meteor slammed here two hundred fourteen million years ago.
The impact carved a huge crater, then the rim filled with water, creating the annular lake.
Inside lies René-Levasseur Island, rising almost a kilometer high with Mount Babel on its summit.
That bright eye you saw is really a scar from a giant space rock.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: Manicouagan Reservoir is a seventy‑kilometer‑wide annular lake formed by a five‑kilometer meteor impact two hundred fourteen million years ago. The crater’s outer ring spans about one hundred kilometers and encloses René‑Levasseur Island, topped by Mount Babel. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics. Photos: NASA, Wikimedia Commons.
